item.title: How does ocean carbon sequestration change under different glacial conditions?
item.description: Over the past 800,000 years, Earth's history has been marked by dramatic shifts in climate, swinging from warm periods to cold, when large ice sheets covered much of the Northern Hemisphere and sea ice greatly expanded. The transition between the two climates is paced by the Earth's orbit with respect to the sun, but changes in the amount of carbon dioxide (CO2), a greenhouse gas, also affect global temperatures. By understanding how CO2 is exchanged between the atmosphere and the ocean, scientists hope to apply that knowledge to future climate scenarios. Fuente: Phys.org.
